name: MCPJam Backend LLM free buckets drained >60/h
description: PAGE · More than 60 free daily buckets were fully drained this hour. Worst legit hour on record is 29.
A drained bucket is a subject that spent its whole free allowance. Real users almost never do; a farm does it on every identity it mints.
TRIAGE — open View Query below, replace the last line with:
guestDailySpendingUtcDay with no ipKey → header-less callers hitting the Convex origin direct
signedInDailySpendingUtcDay at volume → scenario-owner bypass or signup farming
rationale: WHY THIS EXISTS: a drained bucket is a subject that spent its whole free allowance. Ordinary users almost never do; a farm does it on every minted identity. On 09-15 there were 1,770 drained signed-in buckets vs 5-19/day baseline, up to 295/h. The existing 'subject over daily cap' monitors watch this per subject-kind over a UTC day and fire once; this is the hourly, all-buckets version.
WHY THIS THRESHOLD: measured hourly drains 08-25..09-12: max per day 1-16, one 29 (09-11). Abuse hours 200-295. 60 = 2x the worst legit hour.

CONTEXT (2026-09-15 incident): $5,187 of MCPJam-paid spend in one UTC day. Every existing spend monitor fired correctly and posted to #mcpjam-alerts, but each is a single fixed threshold that notifies ONCE on crossing (Axiom threshold monitors only notify on state change; there is no re-notify while open). The daily page said '$107 is above $100' and then stayed silent while the day climbed to $5k, in a channel that also carries Sentry/PostHog/BE5 noise. Fan-out abuse (thousands of minted guests spending $1-3 each) moved the SPENDER COUNT 5-10x before the dollars did. This monitor set adds (a) a ladder of escalating spend tiers so a big day produces escalating messages, and (b) fan-out signals that lead the dollars.
SCOPE: only MCPJam's money — spendingPolicy=consume_mcpjam_limit AND modelSource=mcpjam. BYOK / record_only never cost us and are excluded (the older 'spend velocity' monitors sum everything).
